action: Show the connected fictional library workbench.
narrator: Borrowing one tool is easy. Borrowing a set that actually works together is harder. One missing battery can turn a weekend project into another shopping trip.

action: Ask what Priya needs to build a planter box on Saturday afternoon.
narrator: Priya wants a planter box for her Saturday project. The library, people, and availability shown here are fictional.
assistant: Here’s what you need for the planter box project. Find a kit to check availability; nothing is reserved yet.

action: Find compatible kits and compare bundle cards.
narrator: The alternatives use either a corded drill with an outlet bench or a different cordless platform with its matching battery.
assistant: I found three complete, compatible kits. Each includes the required tools, matching accessories, two clamps, safety glasses, and a bench slot.

action: Choose the first kit and show held item tiles and expiry.
narrator: A temporary hold gives Priya time to decide before committing.
assistant: The complete kit and bench are held for ten simulated minutes. Confirm to book them together.

action: Commit and show the substitution consent dialog, then accept.
narrator: A substitute can change the setup. That choice belongs to the borrower.
assistant: This bundle uses a corded drill that needs the outlet bench. Accept?

action: Show the booked kit and bench timeline.
narrator: The server checks every resource before saving. If any part becomes unavailable during the hold, nothing is booked.
assistant: I booked the complete kit and bench for two to four-thirty p.m. Return every item by five p.m.

action: Reload the client and ask What did I book?.
narrator: Reloading recovers the booking from persisted library state, so Priya can return to the same plan.

action: Report broken clamps and show only their replacement.
narrator: A broken tool should not mean starting the project plan over.
assistant: I swapped your standard clamps for the wide-jaw clamps. Every other item and the bench stay booked.

action: Cancel the booking and show release plus Jonas waitlist outcome.
narrator: Shared tools can support another project as soon as a complete set becomes available.
assistant: All items and the bench were released together. Jonas, on the waitlist, now has a complete booking.

action: Open the Protocol inspector and show initialize, tool traffic, and elicitation.
narrator: This simulated assistant uses a real MCP client and server over Streamable HTTP. A deterministic intent router connects the conversation to tools without a paid language-model API. The inspector shows protocol negotiation, tool calls, and the consent exchange as raw JSON RPC.

action: Return to the workbench with its simulation and fictional-data disclaimer visible.
narrator: BorrowMesh makes the complete working set the unit of borrowing. Local, deterministic, and ready to explore without an account. Simulated Alexa-plus-style experience. Not affiliated with Amazon.
